=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are clearly seen radiating from a single node at the stem apex, with a lower node also showing a cluster)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped together at the top of the short stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade attached to the stem by a petiole)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed (margin is distinctly serrated/serrulate)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): ovate (leaves are broadest below the middle and taper to the apex)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapers to a distinct, elongated point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (wedge-shaped, narrowing towards the petiole)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): prominent and clearly visible, curving towards the leaf margin
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface reflects light, indicating a glabrous/waxy texture)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are clearly visible but relatively short compared to the leaf blade)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): winged (the petioles appear flattened with narrow edges)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears green and succulent, typical of a young seedling)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem appears smooth)
    19.	Stem color: green
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): unclear (node structures are crowded, making distinct stipules hard to confirm)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no distinct jointed structure at the petiole base)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a distinct whorled arrangement of leaves. Several leaves show minor damage in the form of small holes along the margins. The venation is strongly impressed, giving the leaf surface a slightly rugose appearance.
